rationale: Start with a broad, moderately fast gradient to locate all six peaks and identify critical separations while limiting late-elution risk. The midpoint temperature leaves room to tune selectivity in either direction.
Injection 1 already achieved the maximum CRF, with ample resolution margin. Shorten the gradient while holding composition endpoints and temperature fixed to seek a faster fully resolved method.

Shorten the gradient another grid step to test whether full resolution survives at a lower analysis time. The early pair is limiting at R = 2.54, so keep temperature and endpoints unchanged to isolate the slope effect.

Test the minimum gradient duration to establish the speed–resolution boundary, monitoring the early pair now at R = 1.73. Injection 3 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method if this steeper gradient loses resolution.

Return to the shortest fully resolved gradient and raise temperature one experimental step to test faster elution and temperature-dependent selectivity. Monitor the early pair closely because its resolution margin at 40 C was only 0.23.

Lower temperature should improve the critical early-pair selectivity, while reducing phi1 makes the two-minute gradient less steep. Test whether these changes recover full resolution faster than the confirmed four-minute method; the final hold should still elute the last peak comfortably within ten minutes.

Raise the final organic fraction one grid step to accelerate the late peak while retaining the low-temperature selectivity benefit. This tests whether the critical early pair can remain at R ≥ 1.5 despite the slightly steeper gradient; injection 6 is the fallback.

Raise phi0 one grid step to reduce the gradient span while preserving the stronger final solvent that accelerated the last peak. Test whether the shallower slope restores the early pair above R = 1.5 without sacrificing the shorter elution time.

Shift both endpoints upward while retaining the successful 0.70 gradient span and low temperature. This should accelerate the late peak while testing whether the early pair retains full resolution at the stronger starting composition.

Raise phi0 another grid step to seek earlier final elution while retaining full resolution. The first peak is approaching the outlet gradient-arrival time, so this run also tests whether reduced initial retention begins to compress the early pair.
Back off to the fully resolved starting composition and raise temperature by 5 C to accelerate the last peak. This tests whether the early pair's R = 1.77 margin can tolerate modest heating.
Increase temperature one more grid step to locate the full-resolution boundary for this fast gradient. Injection 12 retains the maximum CRF and is the fallback if the early pair drops below R = 1.5.
